RECOMMENDATION: DON'T RAISE IT
LIKELIHOOD: 20

An all-women panel is not evidence of anything. Panels reflect who was available in the department; four women on a hiring committee is unremarkable and proves no motive. If you lead with it, you look like you're inferring bias from demographics alone — which is exactly the reasoning you'd object to if applied to you. It will cost you credibility and likely end the conversation.

Your real case is substantive: you appear stronger on the formal criteria (completed PhD, 6 papers, 4 years teaching), and "industry experience" may or may not have been a weighted criterion in the advertisement. Check the posted criteria, then send a written follow-up demanding the explanation you're entitled to. Argue the criteria, not the committee.
